messages:
dalia: Heads up — we started seeing gRPC streaming stalls from gpu-pool-eu -> gpu-pool-eu this morning around 08:00 UTC. Streams hang ~10-20s then reconnect (clients see transport errors).
odar: I mean Omar: same here, spike in retransmits on the node NICs and app-level "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing" logs. Not all pods affected, looks like subset pinned to certain nodes.
omar: Quick trace: tcpdump on node shows repeated data packets followed by ICMP "frag needed" messages:
```
08:22:13.123456 IP 10.2.3.4.59912 > 10.3.4.5.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1451, ack 1, win 29200, length 1450
08:22:13.123457 IP (frag needed) 192.0.2.1 > 10.2.3.4: ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag needed and DF) mtu 1500
```
That looks like PMTU discovery telling us to fragment but DF set.
dalia: I ran `ping -M do -s 1472 <pod-ip>` between the two nodes — it fails, but succeeds at 1400.
kai: What CNI and tunnel MTU are we using? Calico with VXLAN uses overlay MTU calc = host_mtu - 50 (VXLAN overhead). If host mtu is 9001 (eni jumbo) and we left calico host_mtu default, tunnels might be mis-calculated. Also some cloud ENIs advertise jumbo but underlying path to other nodes isn't jumbo.
marta: Also noticed our egress firewall in front of some nodes drops ICMP type3/code4 (see fw-audit). If ICMP frag-needed isn't getting back to sender, PMTU discovery will blackhole bigger packets -> gRPC streaming stalls when chunked frames exceed the working MTU.
infra-bot: Alert: node/compute-eu-12 reported tx-retransmits increase 6x at 08:17 UTC.
omar: I ran iperf3 with different MSS sizes:
```
# on server node
iperf3 -s
# on client node
iperf3 -c <server> -M 1440 -l 1400 -t 30  -> stable
iperf3 -c <server> -M 1500 -l 1450 -t 30  -> 20% retransmits / stalls
```
So everything above ~1450 fails intermittently.
dalia: Quick mitigation I applied on the affected host nodes: clamp MSS for forwarded TCP so endpoints will avoid oversized segments. Commands used:
```bash
# kernel, ensure PMTU discovery enabled
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0
# MSS clamp on host (temporary) - needs to be applied in the bridge/forward path for pods
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT  -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
# disable TSO/GSO quickly to rule offload issues
ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
```
After those, I saw stream failures drop dramatically on the affected nodes.
kai: Good. Long term we should: 1) ensure CNI calculates overlay MTU from actual path MTU or force a conservative MTU; 2) add MSS clamp either in CNI or kube-proxy/iptables managed rules; 3) allow ICMP frag-needed in firewall.
marta: Root cause summary: cloud ENI advertised jumbo 9001 but some inter-node hops (cloud infra + fw) were limited to 1500 and the firewall was dropping ICMP type3/code4. Combined with DF on tunneled packets, PMTU discovery failed -> blackhole for large gRPC frames. VXLAN/calico overhead + mismatched host MTU made it worse.
omar: Also worth calling out GSO/TSO interactions — when offloads are on, big software segments are handed to NIC and if the NIC cannot actually send the larger frames due to path MTU mismatch you get confusing retransmit patterns. Disabling TSO/GSO on one node reproduced the failure differently.
dalia: Post-mortem actions:
- patch: add `--mtu 1450` to calico/node DaemonSet config in gpu pools where ENI MTU unreliable.
- infra: add iptables TCPMSS clamp as a default in our cluster bootstrap (daemonset) for now.
- network: allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 on egress/ingress ACLs for all cluster subnets.
- observability: new alert on host-level ICMP frag-needed drop counters and TCP retransmit > 1% sustained for 5m.
- perf: run a rollout to test across 3 nodes and watch retransmit and rpc error counts.
kai: I'll add a kube-daemonset manifest to set ethtool offloads per NIC and an init check for path MTU (ping -M do) during node join.
infra-bot: Note: created infra ticket #INFRA-2345 to track calico DaemonSet change and firewall rule request.
dalia: Verified fix: after clamping + firewall change + calico MTU tweak, the affected streams are stable. Retransmits on affected nodes dropped from 2.3% -> 0.1% and gRPC transport errors fell to baseline. Marking this thread resolved.
deploy-bot: Deploy job for calico-mtu-clamp v1.0 started (canary on gpu-pool-eu).
omar: follow-up: we should document recommended host MTU vs overlay MTU mapping and add a unit check to PRs that touch CNI configs.
